summary: Northwest tip of Vancouver Island: an unwatched light on a wooden mast in 1927, a WWII radar site, and a staffed Coast Guard station with a 1981 steel tower.

corrections.why: The 1927 light was an unwatched acetylene light on a wooden mast with a red lantern, not a tower; the 9 m steel skeletal tower carrying the light dates from 1981 (Rowlett; Lighthouse Friends).

corrections.proposed: wooden mast light with red lantern, 1927; steel skeletal tower, 9 m, 1981, standing
corrections.why: The record conflates the 1927 mast with the current tower; the two should be listed separately.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1927 date is the first light, an unwatched acetylene light on a wooden mast (Colonist notice, 29 October 1927). The current light, 1981, is the steel tower. Both are kept in the story.
Lighthouse Friends gives 1959 for the light on the radar foundation with keepers' dwellings; Rowlett gives 1960 for the replacement of the mast light. The story says 1959 and notes Rowlett's 1960.
Lighthouse Friends says most Danish settlers left by 1907; the 101 Squadron history says the settlement ran 1897 to 1917 and that the last resident left in 1956. The story reports both.
Lighthouse Friends' text spells the first keeper William Gardner; its keeper list gives William Edward Gardiner. The story uses the list's spelling.
101 Squadron says the RCAF station was staffed by roughly seventy men on two sites; Lighthouse Friends says roughly fifty men. The story gives both.
Lighthouse Friends says the grounds are open and the tower closed; Rowlett says visitors can climb to the gallery of the tower. The story gives both and does not recommend climbing.

BC Parks says the lighthouse is outside the park and federally operated; Lighthouse Friends says just outside the park; Rowlett says the lighthouse is surrounded by Cape Scott Provincial Park. The story attributes the BC Parks statement.

notes_for_editor: (1) The Marine Department annual reports in the local corpus end in 1924, so the 1927 light rests on the Daily Colonist notice (primary, read in the Internet Archive text) and on Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett. The 2 November 1927 page number is not confirmed (Wikipedia cites p. 12; not checked on the page image). (2) The Colonist notice is signed 'A. W. R. Wilby, Agent Dept. of Marine'; the notice is dated by its 29 October establishment date. (3) Settlement dates conflict: Lighthouse Friends (most gone by 1907) against the 101 Squadron page (1897 to 1917; last resident Alfred Spencer left 1956). Both reported. (4) Radar dates: 101 Squadron gives formed 13 December 1942 and operational 5 February 1943; Lighthouse Friends gives 'abandoned in 1945'. The 1945 closure is from Lighthouse Friends. (5) 1959 against 1960 for the light on the radar foundation (Lighthouse Friends vs Rowlett). (6) Keeper spelling: Gardner (LHF text) vs Gardiner (LHF list). (7) Harvey Humchitt is listed by Lighthouse Friends as keeper from 2004 to at least 2024; named only in that public role, no personal details. (8) Wikipedia was read for leads only; its trail-use statement ('unofficial trails, use discouraged') was not checked against BC Parks and is not used. (9) The Wikipedia footnote cites a 2019 CBC item on solar panels replacing the diesel generators; not checked and not used. (10) The keeper statement 'one of the final three manned lights' is Lighthouse Friends' description. (11) The access statement is from BC Parks, a government source, and was read in full on the hiking page; check it again before any visit guidance is printed. (12) No photos added; the Commons image in the record is unlicensed in the record. (13) Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett are copyrighted; the story paraphrases them, with no more than one short quotation from each. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28 (independent checker): (a) Quote check passed on first run (0 missing). (b) The Colonist notice (masthead WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 2, 1927, a Wednesday; notice text 'established on Cape Scott ... on October 29') is confirmed; it does not mention the mast or lantern, which come from Lighthouse Friends. The notice's page number is still not read. (c) 'Danish families' is not in the sources; the story says 'a group of Danes' and 'Danish settlers' (101 Squadron). (d) Radar size: 101 Squadron says about seventy men; Lighthouse Friends says roughly fifty; both are stated. (e) Tower access: Rowlett says visitors can climb to the gallery; Lighthouse Friends says the tower is closed; the story does not recommend climbing and says the sources disagree. (f) Park status: BC Parks (the most specific source for access) says outside the park; Rowlett says surrounded by the park. The story attributes BC Parks. (g) Staffed status is dated: Lighthouse Friends' keeper list runs to at least 2024; the story no longer says 'is staffed' as a present fact. (h) Alfred Spencer (last resident, left 1956) and the keepers named (Gardiner, Weeden, Humchitt and others) are named only as published sources name them; no personal details are given. (i) Spelling: Lighthouse Friends' text says 'Gardner' and 'Kitmat'; the story uses the keeper-list spelling and 'Kitimat' for the town.
